1	# REVIEW.md — what a reviewer checks on a PR in this repo
2	
3	This repository produces architectural deliverables from code. Review the PR the
4	way a senior detailer reviews a drawing set, not only the way an engineer
5	reviews Python.
6	
7	## Always
8	
9	- **Generated files match the generator.** If `recognition/` or `rules/` changed,
10	  `examples/` must be regenerated in the same PR. If `examples/` changed but no
11	  generator did, ask why.
12	- **No hand edits** to anything under `examples/`, or to `samples/*.ifc`.
13	- **Compliance status did not regress silently.** A model going from `PASS` to
14	  `FAIL`, or findings disappearing, needs an explanation in the PR description.
15	- **Thresholds live in YAML** (`rules/*.yaml`) with a source comment. Flag any
16	  numeric limit hard-coded in `rules.py`.
17	- **Tags are stable.** A diff that renumbers `R-`/`D-`/`W-` tags across a sheet
18	  must be called out in the PR title — it invalidates references on every other
19	  drawing.
20	- **Tests** cover behaviour changes; `uv run pytest -q` is green.
21	
22	## Drawings (`recognition/drawings.py`, `examples/**/sheets/*`)
23	
24	- Dimension chains: segment values sum to the overall dimension; no segments
25	  under 50 mm; stations only on exterior faces and exterior openings.
26	- Door swings open into a room, never into a wall; one arc per door.
27	- Every room has a tag, a name and an area; labels do not sit on walls.
28	- Title block: sheet number, scale, date, revision present; scale actually fits
29	  the sheet (nothing outside the border).
30	- DXF: layers follow the `A-*` naming; units are millimetres.
31	
32	## Rules (`recognition/rules.py`, `rules/*.yaml`)
33	
34	- Each rule records passes and failures (coverage visible in the report).
35	- Rules that cannot be evaluated do not report pass.
36	- Severity `error` is reserved for hard requirements.
37	
38	## Model loading (`recognition/model.py`)
39	
40	- Changes to `ROOM_CATEGORIES` or `_infer_external` affect every downstream
41	  output; expect and check corresponding diffs in `examples/`.
42	- Both IFC2x3 and IFC4 sample models must still load with the same element
43	  counts (`tests/test_pipeline.py::test_inventory`).

1 # Recognition — system architecture 2 3 > **Thesis: the model plans, the code draws.** 4 > Devin never emits geometry and never states a regulation. It fills in a structured 5 > plan; deterministic code turns that plan into a building, and a deterministic rule 6 > engine judges the result. 7 8 Interactive version (diagrams, full tables): **https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7966e4e4-48d4-4909-b472-edaf00fd1b18** 9 10 | | | 11 |---|---| 12 | Geometry source of truth | IFC4 via IfcOpenShell | 13 | Compute | GitHub Actions (secrets stay server-side) | 14 | UI | Static, GitHub Pages, client-side IFC viewer | 15 | Jurisdiction (v1) | Bayern — BayBO Art. 45/46/48 + DIN 18040-2 | 16 | v1 input | Natural language → 2D + 3D. Sketch → 3D is phase 8. | 17 18 Related: [autonomy.md](autonomy.md) · [studio.md](studio.md) · [contracts.md](contracts.md) · [regulations.md](regulations.md) · [adr/](adr/) 19 20 > **Autonomy note.** The interview in L1 below is described as interactive. It is not: 21 > it runs *before* the trigger and produces a sealed brief, after which the run reaches 22 > merged artifacts with nobody in the middle and no approval step. See 23 > [autonomy.md](autonomy.md), which supersedes L1's position. 24 25 --- 26 27 ## 1. The five sources of truth 28 29 Everything else in the repository is *derived* and may be deleted and regenerated. 30 **Nothing derived is ever hand-edited** — not by a human, not by Devin. 31 32 | # | Authority over | Artifact | Written by | Hard rule | 33 |---|---|---|---|---| 34 | SoT-1 | **Intent** | `briefs/.json` | Interview agent, confirmed by user | Never silently inferred; unconfirmed values become recorded `assumptions[]` | 35 | SoT-2 | **Regulation** | `rules/by/*.yaml` | A human curator, with citation | No LLM may author, edit or extend a rule | 36 | SoT-3 | **Geometry** | `design/.py` | The deterministic translator | The only editable geometry artifact | 37 | SoT-4 | **Exchange** | `out/model.ifc` | IfcOpenShell, from SoT-3 | Pure output; regenerated every run | 38 | SoT-5 | **Provenance** | git history + Entire checkpoints | git hooks | Append-only | 39 40 Why the Python DSL and not the IFC is the geometry truth: an IFC diff is unreadable and an 41 agent editing IFC directly can produce a file that parses but is architecturally nonsense. 42 The DSL is ~40 readable lines for a six-room house, every number is a dimension in metres, 43 and a diff shows exactly what moved. That reviewability *is* the safety mechanism. 44 See [ADR-0001](adr/0001-geometry-source-of-truth.md). 45 46 --- 47 48 ## 2. Layers 49 50 Numbering is a real dependency order: L*n* may only read artifacts produced by L*.json` (SoT-1), `questions[]`, `assumptions[]` 70 - **libraries** pydantic, Devin API 71 - **fails when** a returned value falls outside the slot enum/range → rejected and re-asked, never coerced 72 73 ### L2 — Plan synthesis, the architect · *LLM, strongest, temp 0* 74 75 `DesignBrief` in, `ArchitectPlan` out: storeys, rooms with target areas and categories, an 76 adjacency graph, a circulation spine, opening intents. **No coordinates** — the architect 77 reasons in relationships and areas; metres are L3's job. 78 79 Architectural knowledge lives here as retrievable skill files, not model memory: room-size 80 *Richtwerte*, adjacency conventions (bath reached from the hall, not through a bedroom), 81 daylight orientation, circulation width, structural span limits. 82 83 The plan is **pre-checked before geometry exists** — target areas are tested against the 84 ruleset immediately, so "bedroom 6 m² but you asked for barrier-free" costs one cheap call 85 instead of a full geometry round-trip. 86 87 - **reads** `DesignBrief` only — never the chat transcript 88 - **emits** `plans/

.json`, `rationale.md` 89 - **libraries** pydantic, networkx 90 - **fails when** adjacency graph disconnected or areas exceed the footprint → returned with the specific violation 91 92 ### L3 — Deterministic translation · *0 tokens, pure code* 93 94 The heart of the anti-hallucination design, proven by 95 [Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD](https://github.com/Pan-Chera/Multi-Agent-CAD) (MIT): a plain 96 Python function turns the typed plan into DSL source at zero token cost. 97 98 `recognition/translate.py` runs rectangular floor-packing over the adjacency graph, derives 99 wall centre-lines from room boundaries, snaps to a 5 cm grid, and places openings where the 100 plan asked. Constructs it cannot express emit a `# TODO_AGENT:` marker with the plan 101 fragment attached — **only those markers are ever sent to a model.** 102 103 - **emits** `design/

.py` (SoT-3) 104 - **libraries** shapely, networkx, rectpack, black (so diffs stay clean) 105 - **fails when** packing cannot satisfy the adjacency graph → infeasibility report back to L2, never a broken plan 106 107 See [ADR-0002](adr/0002-deterministic-translator.md). 108 109 ### L4 — Geometry kernel & artifacts · *no model* 110 111 Executing the DSL builds real IFC4: `IfcWall` with extruded solids, `IfcSpace` carrying 112 name/category/area, `IfcDoor`/`IfcWindow` cut through proper `IfcOpeningElement`s. 113 Semantics matter — a compliance engine must ask "what is the net floor area of this 114 bedroom", which a mesh cannot answer. Everything else is a serializer off that one IFC. 115 116 - **emits** `model.ifc`, `sheets/*.{svg,pdf,png,dxf}`, `model.glb`, `schedules/*.csv` 117 - **libraries** ifcopenshell, shapely, svgwrite, cairosvg, ezdxf, IfcConvert 118 - **fails when** solids self-intersect or an opening misses its wall → assertion, non-zero exit 119 120 ### L5 — Verification, the arbiter · *the gate* 121 122 Four independent deterministic checks. Devin's work is finished when this layer is green, 123 not when Devin says so. 124 125 1. **Regulation** — `recognition/rules.py` emits one result per element checked, pass *or* 126 fail, so coverage is visible alongside violations. 127 2. **Data completeness** — `ifctester` validates against a buildingSMART **IDS** file: 128 are the properties a checker needs actually present? Catches "the rule passed because 129 the data was missing". 130 3. **Geometry sanity** — shapely: no overlapping rooms, no room without a door, envelope 131 closed, no wall floating free. 132 4. **Regression** — pytest over committed examples; output is deterministic, so an 133 unexplained diff in an untouched sheet *is* the bug signal. 134 135 - **fails when** any `tier: law` rule fails → merge blocked. Guidance-tier failures inform, never block. 136 137 ### L6 — Iteration, options & edit · *LLM, router* 138 139 "Make the Schlafzimmer at least 25 m²" is ambiguous by design. A small classifier routes 140 the request to the **lowest layer that can satisfy it**; it re-enters there, never at the top. 141 142 | Request kind | Example | Re-enters at | Cost | 143 |---|---|---|---| 144 | Rule change | "bedrooms must be ≥ 25 m² under the new code" | L0 — edit YAML, re-run L5 | seconds, no model | 145 | Design change | "make the Schlafzimmer at least 25 m²" | L2 — amend plan, re-translate | one strong call | 146 | Local geometry | "move that wall 600 mm west" | L3 — patch the DSL | zero model | 147 | Drawing only | "show dimensions in cm" | L4 — drawing config | zero model | 148 149 **Options as branches.** When several strategies satisfy a request, each becomes its own git 150 branch with its own sheets, compliance result and cost estimate. Choosing one merges it; 151 the others stay in history. 152 153 ### L7 — Presentation · *no server* 154 155 GitHub Pages serves static files only, so the browser does the viewing work. 156 [`web-ifc`](https://github.com/ThatOpen/engine_web-ifc) (MPL-2.0) parses IFC in WebAssembly 157 and renders through three.js — a real 3D model with no backend. 2D sheets are already 158 vector SVG. **The page never holds a secret.** 159 160 ### L8 — Orchestration & provenance · *infra* 161 162 GitHub Actions is the runtime. Devin is invoked from inside a workflow where the API key 163 lives as a repository secret. Entire captures every agent session and binds it to the commit 164 it produced, so any line of a generated drawing traces back to the conversation that caused 165 it. See [ADR-0004](adr/0004-runtime-topology.md). 166 167 --- 168 169 ## 3. Agent roster 170 171 Each stage reads **only the previous stage's structured JSON — never the conversation 172 history**. That is exactly this role and 185 nothing else in the pipeline. The Interviewer and Architect are short structured-output 186 calls — cheaper and more controllable as direct API calls. 187 188 --- 189 190 ## 4. The interview: a grill that cannot invent 191 192 Questions are generated from the ruleset's declared data requirements, and the gap analysis 193 is Python. 194 195 ```yaml 196 # rules/by/residential.yaml 197 - id: BF-TRIGGER-ART48 198 title: Barrier-free dwellings required 199 tier: law 200 source: 201 law: BayBO Art. 48 (1) 202 url: https://www.gesetze-bayern.de/Content/Document/BayBO-48 203 retrieved: 2026-08-22 204 requires: [dwelling_count, storey_count] # ← drives the interview 205 when: dwelling_count > 2 206 then: { require_ruleset: din-18040-2 } 207 ``` 208 209 At interview time the engine computes `needed = ⋃ rule.requires`, subtracts what the brief 210 holds, and asks about the difference. Add a rule tomorrow and the interview covers it the 211 same day. 212 213 **Four question forms** — `single` (closed enum, so an out-of-set answer is impossible), 214 `multi` (from the room-category vocabulary already in `model.py`), `number` (with unit and 215 plausible range), and `free` text, which is available on every question. 216 217 **Stopping rule** 218 1. Stop when no **blocking** slot is empty — blocking = required by a `tier: law` rule. 219 Legal inputs are never assumed. 220 2. Cap at 3 rounds, ≤ 4 questions per round. 221 3. Every non-blocking slot still empty is written to `assumptions[]` with its default, basis 222 and confidence, then rendered in the UI as an editable chip. 223 224 The assumption register is the honesty surface: the failure mode of design agents is the 225 silent guess — the model picks 2.50 m ceilings, never mentions it, and the client finds out 226 in the drawing. 227 228 --- 229 230 ## 5. Best phase-8 candidate. 273 274 ### Considered and rejected 275 276 | Option | Verdict | Reasoning | 277 |---|---|---| 278 | [OpenSCAD](https://github.com/openscad/openscad) | **not adopted** | Mesh CSG, no B-rep, and decisively **no semantics** — a union cannot tell you a room's category or net floor area, which is exactly what compliance needs. 1	# The Studio — L7, the interface
2	
3	> *"A drawing-office light table. The sheet is the hero; the rest is the instrument
4	> panel."* — the note at the top of the original `style.css`, and still the brief.
5	
6	The Studio is where a person meets the autonomous layer. It has exactly two jobs:
7	take a brief in, and make a building legible coming out. Everything between those
8	two moments happens without it.
9	
10	## Brand
11	
12	Carried forward from the existing UI rather than reinvented — the visual language was
13	already right for the domain and consistency is worth more than novelty.
14	
15	| Token | Value | Role |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `--board` | `#E4E8EC` | the desk the sheet lies on |
18	| `--paper` | `#FFFFFF` | the sheet — always the brightest thing on screen |
19	| `--ink` | `#15191D` | walls, type |
20	| `--accent` | `#2A62D8` | drafting blue: openings, links, the one action |
21	| `--pass` / `--warn` / `--fail` | `#167A4C` / `#B8740A` / `#C8352A` | verdicts, never decoration |
22	| `--font-ui` | Familjen Grotesk | interface |
23	| `--font-mono` | IBM Plex Mono | every number, tag and dimension |
24	
25	Three rules that keep it feeling like a drawing office and not a dashboard:
26	
27	1. **The drawing is the hero.** Panels are quiet; the sheet and the model get the
28	   contrast, the shadow and the space.
29	2. **Numbers are monospace, always.** A room area, a door width, a rule threshold and
30	   a tag are all data, and data lines up.
31	3. **Verdict colour is reserved.** `--pass` / `--fail` mean a compliance result and
32	   nothing else. Nothing decorative is ever green.
33	
34	## The four states
35	
36	### 1 · Brief — the interview
37	
38	Deliberately short. Enough to know intent and the specifications the rules actually
39	need, and not one question more. The whole interview is **five questions**, each with
40	options and a free-text escape:
41	
42	| Question | Why it is asked |
43	|---|---|
44	| What are you building? | selects the building class |
45	| How many homes in it? | **required by BayBO Art. 48** — above two, barrier-free becomes mandatory |
46	| Which rooms, and how many? | the programme |
47	| How big is the plot? | bounds the envelope |
48	| Anything else? | free text, always available |
49	
50	Only questions a `tier: law` rule genuinely needs are blocking. Everything else has a
51	default that is recorded as an **assumption** and shown as an editable chip:
52	
53	```
54	ceiling 2.50 m · assumed · BayBO Art. 45 (1) minimum 2.40 m + 100 mm build-up   ✎
55	```
56	
57	The question list is not hand-written. It is derived from the `requires:` fields of
58	the rules in force, so adding a rule adds its question. See
59	[autonomy.md](autonomy.md) for why this runs *before* the trigger.
60	
61	### 2 · Working
62	
63	The layer stack ticks L2 → L5, each step showing the artifact as it appears. When
64	Devin is running, its own words are shown rather than a spinner — the wait is more
65	tolerable when you can see what it is doing.
66	
67	### 3 · Result
68	
69	Three panes: **3D**, **2D sheet**, **findings**.
70	
71	- **3D** — orbit, zoom, hover a room for its tag and area. Walls, spaces, doors and
72	  windows are separately coloured; doors and windows use the accent so the openings
73	  read at a glance.
74	- **2D** — the generated sheet, the same file that goes to a contractor.
75	- **Findings** — grouped by tier. Every entry links to the statute article it came
76	  from, with the retrieval date. Nothing appears without a citation.
77	
78	The stamp always carries coverage. `PASS 57/57` alone is a lie of omission; the
79	Studio renders `57 checked · 2 not evaluated · 0 failed` and lists what it could not
80	see.
81	
82	### 4 · Options
83	
84	When a run explored several strategies, each is a card with its plan, its verdict and
85	its metrics. The winner is already marked — chosen by the scorer, not by the person
86	looking at the screen. Selecting another is a *new trigger*, not an approval.
87	
88	## How 3D works, and why it is static
89	
90	`ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape` triangulates every wall, space, door and window
91	server-side into `mesh.json` — vertices, faces, tag, class, storey per element. The
92	browser loads that JSON and renders it with Three.js.
93	
94	This approach comes from the Studio work on the `studio` branch and is better than the
95	alternative for our case:
96	
97	| | mesh.json + Three.js | web-ifc (WASM) |
98	|---|---|---|
99	| Parses IFC in the browser | no — already triangulated | yes |
100	| Payload | small, only what is drawn | the whole IFC |
101	| Needs a server at view time | **no** | no |
102	| Element tags and areas | carried in the JSON | must be re-derived |
103	
104	Because meshing happens once, when the artifact is produced, the viewer is a static
105	file reading a static file — which is what makes the whole Studio hostable on GitHub
106	Pages with no backend and no secret in the browser.
107	
108	## Hosting
109	
110	GitHub Pages serves `web/` as static files. A run publishes its artifacts into
111	`web/data/<project>/`, and the Studio reads them:
112	
113	```
114	web/
115	  index.html          the Studio
116	  studio.css          brand tokens + layout
117	  studio.js           viewer, interview, state
118	  data/
119	    index.json        which projects exist
120	    <project>/
121	      mesh.json  sheet.svg  verdict.json  plan.json  design.py
122	```
123	
124	The page never holds a secret. A live run is a `repository_dispatch` posted with the
125	viewer's own credentials, or — for the common case — the Studio simply reads the
126	artifacts a previous run already committed.
127	
128	## What the Studio deliberately does not have
129	
130	No **Approve**, no **Reject**, no **Request changes** on the autonomous path. Those
131	made the previous UI a copilot. A person can start a run and can start another one;
132	they cannot hand-approve a building into existence, because the verifier already
133	decided and it does not need a second opinion.
134

=== autopilot.yml ===
# The trigger. Everything after this point runs with nobody in the middle.
#
# Three ways in, all the same pipeline:
#   * repository_dispatch  -- what the web UI posts (the browser holds no secret)
#   * workflow_dispatch    -- a human starting a run from the Actions tab
#   * push to briefs/**    -- committing a brief is itself a trigger
#
# The job never asks for approval. `recognition autopilot` exits non-zero when no
# candidate clears the compliance gate, and that exit code is the gate: a run that
# fails produces no merge, and a run that passes merges itself.
name: autopilot

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types: [design-request]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      brief:
        description: Path to a DesignBrief JSON in the repo
        required: true
        default: briefs/familienhaus.json
      engine:
        description: local (deterministic) or devin (one session per strategy)
        required: true
        default: local
        type: choice
        options: [local, devin]
      strategies:
        description: Comma-separated subset, blank for all
        required: false
        default: ""
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
    paths: ["briefs/**.json"]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: autopilot-${{ github.event.client_payload.brief || inputs.brief || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  design:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Resolve the trigger
        id: cfg
        run: |
          BRIEF="${{ github.event.client_payload.brief || inputs.brief }}"
          ENGINE="${{ github.event.client_payload.engine || inputs.engine }}"
          STRATS="${{ github.event.client_payload.strategies || inputs.strategies }}"
          # A push to briefs/** carries no inputs: design whatever changed.
          if [ -z "$BRIEF" ]; then
            BRIEF=$(git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD -- 'briefs/*.json' | head -1)
          fi
          [ -z "$BRIEF" ] && BRIEF=briefs/familienhaus.json
          [ -z "$ENGINE" ] && ENGINE=local
          echo "brief=$BRIEF"       >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "engine=$ENGINE"     >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "strategies=$STRATS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "slug=$(basename "$BRIEF" .json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # cairosvg needs the native cairo library; without it sheet rendering dies
      # with a dlopen error that looks nothing like a missing apt package.
      - name: System libraries
        run: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq libcairo2

      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
        with:
          enable-cache: true
      - run: uv sync

      - name: Verifier must be green before it may design anything
        run: uv run pytest -q

      - name: Autopilot
        id: run
        env:
          DEVIN_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEVIN_API_KEY }}
          DEVIN_ORG_ID: ${{ secrets.DEVIN_ORG_ID }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          uv run recognition autopilot "${{ steps.cfg.outputs.brief }}" \
            --engine "${{ steps.cfg.outputs.engine }}" \
            --out out/autopilot \
            ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.strategies && format('--strategies {0}', steps.cfg.outputs.strategies) || '' }} \
            2>&1 | tee autopilot.log
          echo "winner=$(jq -r '.winner // ""' out/autopilot/*/run.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Publish the artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: design-${{ steps.cfg.outputs.slug }}
          path: |
            out/autopilot/**
            autopilot.log
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # Auto-merge on green. There is no approval step and no Approve button:
      # the deterministic verifier is the only gate, and it has already run.
      - name: Open and merge the winning design
        if: success() && steps.run.outputs.winner != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          SLUG="${{ steps.cfg.outputs.slug }}"
          WINNER="${{ steps.run.outputs.winner }}"
          BRANCH="design/${SLUG}-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          git config user.name  "recognition-autopilot"
          git config user.email "autopilot@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -b "$BRANCH"
          mkdir -p "deliveries/${SLUG}"
          cp -r out/autopilot/*/"${WINNER}"/. "deliveries/${SLUG}/"
          git add "deliveries/${SLUG}"
          git commit -m "design(${SLUG}): ${WINNER} — passed the compliance gate

          Produced by the autopilot with no human in the loop. The winning
          candidate was chosen by recognition.score, not by a person.

          Run: ${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          git push -u origin "$BRANCH"
          gh pr create --title "design(${SLUG}): ${WINNER}" \
            --body "$(cat out/autopilot/*/"${WINNER}"/verdict.json | jq -r \
              '"**" + .stamp_line + "**"' 2>/dev/null || echo "Autopilot result — see the run artifacts.")

          Winner \`${WINNER}\` cleared every \`tier: law\` rule. Merging automatically." \
            --base main --head "$BRANCH"
          gh pr merge "$BRANCH" --squash --admin --delete-branch

      - name: Report a failed gate honestly
        if: failure()
        run: |
          echo "::error::No candidate cleared the compliance gate. Nothing was merged."
          tail -40 autopilot.log 2>/dev/null || true
=== pages.yml ===
# Publish the Studio to GitHub Pages.
#
# The Studio is static: it reads artifacts a run already committed under
# web/data/. So deploying is just uploading web/ — no build step, no server,
# and no secret ever reaches the browser.
#
# Enable once in Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions.
name: pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["web/**", ".github/workflows/pages.yml"]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Never cancel a half-finished deploy; let the running one land first.
concurrency:
  group: pages
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Fail loudly if the Studio has no data to show
        run: |
          if [ ! -f web/data/index.json ]; then
            echo "::error::web/data/index.json is missing — publish a run first:"
            echo "::error::  uv run recognition autopilot briefs/<name>.json --publish"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "projects:"; jq -r '.projects[] | "  - \(.project) (\(.candidates) layouts, winner: \(.winner))"' web/data/index.json

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: web
      - id: deploy
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

2	
3	    from recognition.design import House
4	
5	    h = House("My house")
6	    eg = h.storey("Erdgeschoss", elevation=0.0, height=2.5)
7	    eg.wall("W1", (0, 0), (12, 0), thickness=0.30, external=True)
8	    eg.room("Küche", [(0.3, 0.3), (4.7, 0.3), (4.7, 4.2), (0.3, 4.2)])

11	    h.write("out/house.ifc")           # 3D: IfcWall / IfcSpace / IfcDoor / IfcWindow with real solids
12	    h.axonometric("out/house.png")     # a quick 3D view

15	Coordinates are metres in the storey plane (x east, y north); walls are
16	centre-lines; `at` is the distance from the wall's start to the opening's
17	centre. The IFC is deliberately plain — extruded solids, openings cut into
18	walls, standard psets — so any viewer or CAD tool reads it and
19	``recognition.model.load`` gets the same walls, rooms, doors and windows

39	@dataclass
40	class Wall:
41	    name: str
42	    start: Pt
43	    end: Pt
44	    thickness: float
45	    height: float
46	    external: bool
47	    entity: ifcopenshell.entity_instance
48	
49	    @property
50	    def length(self) -> float:
51	        return math.dist(self.start, self.end)
52	
53	    @property
54	    def direction(self) -> Pt:
55	        L = self.length
56	        return ((self.end[0] - self.start[0]) / L, (self.end[1] - self.start[1]) / L)
57	
58	    @property
59	    def normal(self) -> Pt:
60	        d = self.direction
61	        return (-d[1], d[0])
62	
63	    def footprint(self, extend: float = 0.0) -> list[Pt]:
64	        d, n, t = self.direction, self.normal, self.thickness / 2
65	        s = (self.start[0] - d[0] * extend, self.start[1] - d[1] * extend)
66	        e = (self.end[0] + d[0] * extend, self.end[1] + d[1] * extend)
67	        return [(s[0] + n[0] * t, s[1] + n[1] * t), (e[0] + n[0] * t, e[1] + n[1] * t),
68	                (e[0] - n[0] * t, e[1] - n[1] * t), (s[0] - n[0] * t, s[1] - n[1] * t)]
69	
70	    def slot(self, at: float, width: float, depth: float) -> list[Pt]:
71	        """Rectangle on the wall axis centred `at` metres from the start, `width` along, `depth` across."""
72	        d, n = self.direction, self.normal
73	        c = (self.start[0] + d[0] * at, self.start[1] + d[1] * at)
74	        w, t = width / 2, depth / 2
75	        return [(c[0] - d[0] * w + n[0] * t, c[1] - d[1] * w + n[1] * t), (c[0] + d[0] * w + n[0] * t, c[1] + d[1] * w + n[1] * t),
76	                (c[0] + d[0] * w - n[0] * t, c[1] + d[1] * w - n[1] * t), (c[0] - d[0] * w - n[0] * t, c[1] - d[1] * w - n[1] * t)]

84	    height: float

90	    def wall(self, name: str, start: Pt, end: Pt, thickness: float = 0.30, height: float | None = None,
91	             external: bool = False) -> Wall:
92	        if name in self.walls:
93	            raise ValueError(f"wall {name!r} already exists on {self.name}")
94	        h = height or self.height
95	        ent = self.house._product("IfcWall", name)
96	        wall = Wall(name, tuple(start), tuple(end), thickness, h, external, ent)
97	        self.house._solid(ent, wall.footprint(extend=thickness / 2), self.elevation, h)
98	        run("spatial.assign_container", self.house.f, relating_structure=self.entity, products=[ent])
99	        self.house._pset(ent, "Pset_WallCommon", {"IsExternal": external, "LoadBearing": external})
100	        self.walls[name] = wall
101	        return wall

103	    def room(self, name: str, polygon: list[Pt], height: float | None = None, tag: str | None = None) -> ifcopenshell.entity_instance:
104	        """A room as its floor outline. The name drives the category (Küche → kitchen …)."""
105	        ent = self.house._product("IfcSpace", tag or name)
106	        ent.LongName = name
107	        ent.PredefinedType = "INTERNAL"
108	        self.house._solid(ent, list(polygon), self.elevation, height or self.height)
109	        run("aggregate.assign_object", self.house.f, relating_object=self.entity, products=[ent])
110	        self.rooms.append(ent)

113	    def door(self, name: str, on: str, at: float, width: float = 0.885, height: float = 2.01, sill: float = 0.0,
114	             external: bool | None = None, type_name: str = "") -> ifcopenshell.entity_instance:
115	        return self._opening("IfcDoor", name, on, at, width, height, sill, external, type_name)
116	
117	    def window(self, name: str, on: str, at: float, width: float = 1.2, height: float = 1.2, sill: float = 0.9,
118	               external: bool | None = None, type_name: str = "") -> ifcopenshell.entity_instance:
119	        return self._opening("IfcWindow", name, on, at, width, height, sill, external, type_name)

121	    def _opening(self, ifc_class, name, on, at, width, height, sill, external, type_name):
122	        wall = self.walls.get(on)
123	        if wall is None:
124	            raise ValueError(f"no wall {on!r} on {self.name}; have {sorted(self.walls)}")
125	        if not 0 < at < wall.length:
126	            raise ValueError(f"{name}: at={at} is outside wall {on} (length {wall.length:.2f})")
127	        f = self.house.f
128	        z = self.elevation + sill
129	        hole = self.house._product("IfcOpeningElement", f"{name} opening")
130	        self.house._solid(hole, wall.slot(at, width, wall.thickness + 0.04), z, height)
131	        run("feature.add_feature", f, feature=hole, element=wall.entity)
132	        ent = self.house._product(ifc_class, name)
133	        self.house._solid(ent, wall.slot(at, width, max(0.05, wall.thickness / 2)), z, height)
134	        ent.OverallWidth, ent.OverallHeight = float(width), float(height)
135	        if ifc_class == "IfcDoor":
136	            ent.PredefinedType = "DOOR"
137	        run("feature.add_filling", f, opening=hole, element=ent)
138	        run("spatial.assign_container", f, relating_structure=self.entity, products=[ent])
139	        if type_name:
140	            typ = run("root.create_entity", f, ifc_class=ifc_class + "Type", name=type_name)
141	            run("type.assign_type", f, related_objects=[ent], relating_type=typ)
142	        self.house._pset(ent, "Pset_DoorCommon" if ifc_class == "IfcDoor" else "Pset_WindowCommon",
143	                         {"IsExternal": wall.external if external is None else external})
144	        self.openings.append(ent)
145	        return ent

149	    def __init__(self, name: str, schema: str = "IFC4"):
150	        self.name = name
151	        f = self.f = run("project.create_file", version=schema)
152	        self.project = run("root.create_entity", f, ifc_class="IfcProject", name=name)
153	        run("unit.assign_unit", f)  # SI: metres
154	        ctx = run("context.add_context", f, context_type="Model")
155	        self.body = run("context.add_context", f, context_type="Model", context_identifier="Body",
156	                        target_view="MODEL_VIEW", parent=ctx)
157	        self.site = run("root.create_entity", f, ifc_class="IfcSite", name="Site")
158	        self.building = run("root.create_entity", f, ifc_class="IfcBuilding", name=name)
159	        run("aggregate.assign_object", f, relating_object=self.project, products=[self.site])
160	        run("aggregate.assign_object", f, relating_object=self.site, products=[self.building])
161	        self.storeys: list[Storey] = []
162	
163	    # --- authoring -------------------------------------------------------
164	
165	    def storey(self, name: str, elevation: float = 0.0, height: float = 2.5) -> Storey:
166	        ent = run("root.create_entity", self.f, ifc_class="IfcBuildingStorey", name=name)
167	        ent.Elevation = float(elevation)
168	        run("aggregate.assign_object", self.f, relating_object=self.building, products=[ent])
169	        st = Storey(self, name, float(elevation), float(height), ent)

173	    def write(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
174	        path = Path(path)
175	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
176	        self.f.write(str(path))
177	        return path

179	    def axonometric(self, path: str | Path, scale: float = 40.0) -> Path:
180	        return axonometric(self.f, path, scale=scale, title=self.name)

182	    # --- ifc plumbing ------------------------------------------------------
183	
184	    def _product(self, ifc_class: str, name: str):
185	        return run("root.create_entity", self.f, ifc_class=ifc_class, name=name)
186	
187	    def _solid(self, product, polygon: list[Pt], z: float, height: float) -> None:
188	        pts = [(float(x), float(y)) for x, y in polygon]
189	        if pts[0] != pts[-1]:
190	            pts.append(pts[0])
191	        profile = run("profile.add_arbitrary_profile", self.f, profile=pts, name=product.Name)
192	        rep = run("geometry.add_profile_representation", self.f, context=self.body, profile=profile, depth=float(height))
193	        m = np.eye(4)
194	        m[2, 3] = float(z)
195	        run("geometry.edit_object_placement", self.f, product=product, matrix=m)
196	        run("geometry.assign_representation", self.f, product=product, representation=rep)
197	
198	    def _pset(self, product, name: str, props: dict) -> None:
199	        pset = run("pset.add_pset", self.f, product=product, name=name)
200	        run("pset.edit_pset", self.f, pset=pset, properties=props)

203	# --- a quick 3D view ----------------------------------------------------------
204	
205	COLOURS = {"IfcWall": "#6B7480", "IfcDoor": "#B5651D", "IfcWindow": "#2F6FE4", "IfcSpace": "#DCE6F5"}
206	
207	
208	def axonometric(ifc: ifcopenshell.file | str | Path, path: str | Path, scale: float = 40.0, title: str = "") -> Path:
209	    """Isometric projection of walls, doors and windows (rooms as floor tints), painter-sorted. PNG via SVG."""
210	    f = ifc if isinstance(ifc, ifcopenshell.file) else ifcopenshell.open(str(ifc))
211	    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
212	    settings.set("use-world-coords", True)
213	    c30, s30 = math.cos(math.radians(30)), math.sin(math.radians(30))
214	    faces = []  # (depth, points2d, colour, shade)
215	    for cls, colour in COLOURS.items():
216	        for el in f.by_type(cls):
217	            try:
218	                shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, el)
219	            except Exception:
220	                continue
221	            v, fc = shape.geometry.verts, shape.geometry.faces
222	            pts = [(v[i], v[i + 1], v[i + 2]) for i in range(0, len(v), 3)]
223	            if cls == "IfcSpace":  # floor only
224	                z0 = min(p[2] for p in pts)
225	                pts = [p for p in pts if abs(p[2] - z0) < 1e-6]
226	            for i in range(0, len(fc), 3):
227	                tri = [pts[fc[i]], pts[fc[i + 1]], pts[fc[i + 2]]] if cls != "IfcSpace" else None
228	                if tri is None:
229	                    break
230	                a, b, c = (np.array(p) for p in tri)
231	                n = np.cross(b - a, c - a)
232	                if np.linalg.norm(n) < 1e-9:
233	                    continue
234	                n = n / np.linalg.norm(n)
235	                shade = 0.62 + 0.38 * max(0.0, float(np.dot(n, [0.3, -0.5, 0.81])))
236	                faces.append((sum(p[0] + p[1] + p[2] * 0.5 for p in tri), tri, colour, shade))
237	            if cls == "IfcSpace" and pts:
238	                xs = sorted(set(pts))
239	                from shapely.geometry import MultiPoint
240	                hull = MultiPoint([(p[0], p[1]) for p in xs]).convex_hull
241	                if hull.geom_type == "Polygon":
242	                    z0 = pts[0][2]
243	                    poly = [(x, y, z0 + 0.01) for x, y in hull.exterior.coords]
244	                    faces.append((-1e9, poly, colour, 1.0))
245	
246	    def proj(p):
247	        return ((p[0] - p[1]) * c30 * scale, -((p[0] + p[1]) * s30 + p[2]) * scale)
248	
249	    faces.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
250	    projected = [([proj(p) for p in poly], col, sh) for _, poly, col, sh in faces]
251	    xs = [x for poly, _, _ in projected for x, _ in poly]
252	    ys = [y for poly, _, _ in projected for _, y in poly]
253	    pad = 30
254	    minx, miny = min(xs) - pad, min(ys) - pad
255	    W, H = max(xs) - minx + pad, max(ys) - miny + pad + (28 if title else 0)
256	    dwg = svgwrite.Drawing(size=(W, H))
257	    dwg.add(dwg.rect((0, 0), (W, H), fill="white"))
258	    for poly, col, sh in projected:
259	        r, g, b = (int(col[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5))
260	        fill = f"rgb({int(r * sh)},{int(g * sh)},{int(b * sh)})"
261	        dwg.add(dwg.polygon([(x - minx, y - miny) for x, y in poly], fill=fill, stroke=fill, stroke_width=0.4))
262	    if title:
263	        dwg.add(dwg.text(title, insert=(pad, H - 10), font_size=13, font_family="Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif", fill="#59646E"))
264	    path = Path(path)
265	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
266	    cairosvg.svg2png(bytestring=dwg.tostring().encode("utf-8"), write_to=str(path), background_color="white")
267	    return path

2	
3	The org's key is a legacy `apk_user_` key: the v3 endpoints return 403 for it and
4	v1 works, so v1 is what this speaks. The version lives in one constant.
5	
6	Two v1 quirks that will bite anyone reading this later:
7	
8	* A finished session reports ``status_enum: "blocked"`` *with* ``structured_output``
9	  populated. It never reports "finished". Treating "blocked" as failure will hang
10	  the orchestrator forever.
11	* Attachment upload returns a bare text URL, which goes into the prompt as an
12	  ``ATTACHMENT:"<url>"`` line rather than a JSON field.
13	
14	Nothing in this module decides whether work is good. It starts sessions, polls
15	them, and reports what they produced; `recognition.score` is the only judge.
16	"""
17	from __future__ import annotations

19	import json
20	import os
21	import time
22	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
23	from pathlib import Path
24	from typing import Any, Callable

28	DEVIN_API = "https://api.devin.ai/v1"

30	# A session is done when it is blocked *and* has handed back structured output.
31	TERMINAL = ("blocked", "finished", "expired", "stopped")

38	def extract_json(text: str) -> dict | None:
39	    """Pull the first JSON object out of an agent message.
40	
41	    Handles a ```json fence and a bare object, and tolerates prose either side.
42	    Returns None rather than raising: a message with no JSON in it is a normal
43	    outcome (the session asked a question), not an error.
44	    """
45	    if not text:
46	        return None
47	    fence = text.find("```")
48	    if fence != -1:
49	        rest = text[fence + 3:]
50	        if rest[:4].lower().startswith("json"):
51	            rest = rest[4:]
52	        end = rest.find("```")
53	        candidate = rest[:end] if end != -1 else rest
54	        try:
55	            v = json.loads(candidate.strip())
56	            if isinstance(v, dict):
57	                return v
58	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
59	            pass
60	    start = text.find("{")
61	    while start != -1:
62	        depth, in_str, esc = 0, False, False
63	        for i in range(start, len(text)):
64	            ch = text[i]
65	            if in_str:
66	                if esc:
67	                    esc = False
68	                elif ch == "\\":
69	                    esc = True
70	                elif ch == '"':
71	                    in_str = False
72	                continue
73	            if ch == '"':
74	                in_str = True
75	            elif ch == "{":
76	                depth += 1
77	            elif ch == "}":
78	                depth -= 1
79	                if depth == 0:
80	                    try:

91	class SessionResult:
92	    """What one Devin session produced. No judgement attached."""
93	    session_id: str
94	    status: str = "unknown"
95	    structured_output: dict | None = None
96	    pull_request_url: str = ""
97	    branch: str = ""
98	    last_message: str = ""
99	    error: str = ""

101	    @property
102	    def done(self) -> bool:
103	        if self.error:
104	            return True
105	        if self.status in ("expired", "stopped", "finished"):
106	            return True
107	        # The important one: blocked + structured output means success in v1.
108	        return self.status == "blocked" and self.structured_output is not None
109

111	    def produced_output(self) -> bool:

115	class DevinClient:
116	    """Thin, synchronous v1 client. One method per endpoint we actually use."""
117	
118	    def __init__(self, api_key: str | None = None, *, base: str = DEVIN_API,
119	                 timeout: float = 60.0) -> None:
120	        key = api_key or os.environ.get("DEVIN_API_KEY", "")
121	        if not key:
122	            raise DevinError(
123	                "No Devin API key. Set DEVIN_API_KEY in the environment or a local .env "
124	                "(never commit it), or run the pipeline with --engine local."
125	            )
126	        self._key = key
127	        self.base = base.rstrip("/")
128	        self._http = httpx.Client(
129	            timeout=timeout,
130	            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"},
131	        )
132	
133	    # -- endpoints ---------------------------------------------------------
134	
135	    def create_session(self, prompt: str, *, title: str | None = None,
136	                       playbook_id: str | None = None, tags: list[str] | None = None,
137	                       max_acu: int | None = None,
138	                       structured_output: dict | str | None = None) -> str:
139	        body: dict[str, Any] = {"prompt": prompt}
140	        if title:
141	            body["title"] = title[:120]
142	        if playbook_id:
143	            body["playbook_id"] = playbook_id
144	        if tags:
145	            body["tags"] = tags
146	        if max_acu is not None:
147	            body["max_acu_limit"] = max_acu
148	        if structured_output is not None:
149	            body["structured_output"] = (
150	                structured_output if isinstance(structured_output, str)
151	                else json.dumps(structured_output)
152	            )
153	        r = self._http.post(f"{self.base}/sessions", json=body)
154	        if r.status_code >= 400:
155	            raise DevinError(f"create_session failed ({r.status_code}): {r.text[:400]}")
156	        sid = r.json().get("session_id")
157	        if not sid:
158	            raise DevinError(f"create_session returned no session_id: {r.text[:300]}")
159	        return sid
160	
161	    def get_session(self, session_id: str) -> dict:
162	        r = self._http.get(f"{self.base}/session/{session_id}")
163	        if r.status_code >= 400:
164	            raise DevinError(f"get_session failed ({r.status_code}): {r.text[:300]}")
165	        return r.json()
166	
167	    def send_message(self, session_id: str, text: str) -> None:
168	        r = self._http.post(f"{self.base}/session/{session_id}/message",
169	                            json={"message": text})
170	        if r.status_code >= 400:
171	            raise DevinError(f"send_message failed ({r.status_code}): {r.text[:300]}")
172	
173	    def upload_attachment(self, path: str | Path) -> str:
174	        """Returns a bare URL string, which belongs in the prompt as ATTACHMENT:"…"."""
175	        p = Path(path)
176	        with p.open("rb") as fh:
177	            r = httpx.post(f"{self.base}/attachments",
178	                           headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self._key}"},
179	                           files={"file": (p.name, fh)}, timeout=120.0)
180	        if r.status_code >= 400:
181	            raise DevinError(f"upload_attachment failed ({r.status_code}): {r.text[:300]}")
182	        return r.text.strip().strip('"')
183	
184	    def close(self) -> None:
185	        self._http.close()
186	
187	    # -- polling -----------------------------------------------------------
188	
189	    def snapshot(self, session_id: str) -> SessionResult:
190	        try:
191	            s = self.get_session(session_id)
192	        except DevinError as e:
193	            return SessionResult(session_id, status="error", error=str(e))
194	        so = s.get("structured_output")
195	        if isinstance(so, str):
196	            try:
197	                so = json.loads(so)
198	            except json.JSONDecodeError:
199	                so = {"raw": so}
200	        pr = s.get("pull_request") or {}
201	        msgs = s.get("messages") or []
202	        last = ""
203	        last_full = ""
204	        for m in reversed(msgs):
205	            if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get("message") and m.get("type") != "initial_user_message":
206	                last_full = str(m["message"])
207	                last = last_full[:800]
208	                break
209	
210	        # Observed in v1: a session can answer correctly in a normal message and
211	        # never populate structured_output at all. Waiting on that field alone
212	        # hangs the run until timeout, so recover the payload from the message.
213	        if not isinstance(so, dict) and last_full:
214	            so = extract_json(last_full)
215	        return SessionResult(
216	            session_id=session_id,
217	            status=str(s.get("status_enum") or s.get("status") or "unknown"),
218	            structured_output=so if isinstance(so, dict) else None,
219	            pull_request_url=str(pr.get("url", "") or ""),
220	            branch=str(s.get("branch_name", "") or ""),
221	            last_message=last,
222	        )

226	# Fan-out

229	@dataclass
230	class SessionSpec:
231	    """One candidate to explore. `strategy` is what makes the siblings differ."""
232	    name: str
233	    strategy: str
234	    prompt: str
235	    tags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
236	    max_acu: int | None = None
237	
238	
239	def fan_out(client: DevinClient, specs: list[SessionSpec], *,
240	            structured_output: dict | str | None = None,
241	            playbook_id: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
242	    """Start every session up front so they explore concurrently.
243	
244	    Returns {spec.name: session_id}. A session that fails to start is recorded as
245	    an empty id rather than aborting its siblings -- one dead candidate must not
246	    take the run down.
247	    """
248	    ids: dict[str, str] = {}
249	    for spec in specs:
250	        try:
251	            ids[spec.name] = client.create_session(
252	                spec.prompt, title=f"Recognition · {spec.name}",
253	                playbook_id=playbook_id, tags=spec.tags or ["recognition", "autopilot"],
254	                max_acu=spec.max_acu, structured_output=structured_output,
255	            )
256	        except DevinError as e:
257	            ids[spec.name] = ""
258	            print(f"  ! session '{spec.name}' failed to start: {e}")
259	    return ids
260	
261	
262	def wait_all(client: DevinClient, ids: dict[str, str], *, timeout_s: float = 1800,
263	             interval_s: float = 15.0,
264	             on_update: Callable[[str, SessionResult], None] | None = None,
265	             ) -> dict[str, SessionResult]:
266	    """Poll every live session until each is done or the whole run times out.
267	
268	    Timing out is a normal outcome, not an exception: the orchestrator scores
269	    whatever finished. A slow sibling must never block a good answer.
270	    """
271	    results: dict[str, SessionResult] = {
272	        name: SessionResult(sid, status="error" if not sid else "starting",
273	                            error="" if sid else "session did not start")
274	        for name, sid in ids.items()
275	    }
276	    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
277	    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
278	        pending = [n for n, r in results.items() if not r.done]
279	        if not pending:
280	            break
281	        for name in pending:
282	            snap = client.snapshot(results[name].session_id)
283	            if snap.status != results[name].status or snap.done:
284	                if on_update:
285	                    on_update(name, snap)
286	            results[name] = snap
287	        if all(r.done for r in results.values()):
288	            break
289	        time.sleep(interval_s)
290	    for name, r in results.items():
291	        if not r.done and not r.error:
292	            r.error = f"timed out after {timeout_s:.0f}s in status '{r.status}'"
293	    return results

251	    """Can this rule be decided from the model at all?

253	    Two kinds of rule legitimately have no geometric predicate:
254	      * `checkable: no`  -- the model carries no such data (smoke detectors,
255	        thresholds). Reported as NOT EVALUATED by recognition.score.
256	      * policy triggers (`when:`) -- these select other rulesets from the brief
257	        rather than judging geometry.
258	    Skipping them here is not hiding them: score.verdict() reports every one.
259	    """

261	    if isinstance(checkable, bool):

263	    if str(checkable).lower() in ("no", "false"):
264	        return False

=== mesh.py ===
"""Triangulate an IFC model into JSON the browser can draw.

Adapted from the Studio viewer on the `studio` branch, moved out of the FastAPI
app and into the pipeline. That move is the point: meshing at *artifact* time,
not at view time, is what lets the Studio be a static file reading a static file.
No server runs when someone looks at a building.

The JSON keeps each element separate and carries its tag, class and storey, so
the viewer can colour walls differently from openings and show a room's tag on
hover without re-deriving anything from the IFC.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import ifcopenshell.geom

from . import model as M


def _settings() -> ifcopenshell.geom.settings:
    s = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    s.set("use-world-coords", True)      # so element coords compose without transforms
    return s


def _triangles(settings, entity) -> tuple[list[float], list[int]] | None:
    """Vertices and faces for one element, or None if it has no drawable shape."""
    try:
        shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, entity)
    except Exception:
        # An element without a representation is normal (a space can be a volume
        # with no body). Skipping it is correct; failing the build is not.
        return None
    verts = [round(v, 4) for v in shape.geometry.verts]
    faces = [int(i) for i in shape.geometry.faces]
    return (verts, faces) if verts and faces else None


def build(model_path: str | Path) -> dict:
    """Mesh every wall, space, door and window, tagged as in the schedules."""
    m = M.load(Path(model_path))
    settings = _settings()
    elements: list[dict] = []
    lo = [float("inf")] * 3
    hi = [float("-inf")] * 3

    groups = (
        ("IfcWall", m.walls, lambda e: e.name),
        ("IfcSpace", m.spaces, lambda e: e.label),
        ("IfcDoor", m.doors, lambda e: e.name),
        ("IfcWindow", m.windows, lambda e: e.name),
    )
    for cls, items, name_of in groups:
        for el in items:
            tri = _triangles(settings, m.ifc.by_guid(el.guid))
            if tri is None:
                continue
            verts, faces = tri
            for i in range(0, len(verts), 3):
                for k in range(3):
                    v = verts[i + k]
                    lo[k] = min(lo[k], v)
                    hi[k] = max(hi[k], v)
            entry = {
                "tag": el.tag, "name": name_of(el), "cls": cls,
                "storey": el.storey, "verts": verts, "faces": faces,
            }
            if cls == "IfcSpace":
                entry["area"] = round(getattr(el, "area", 0.0), 2)
                entry["category"] = getattr(el, "category", "other")
            elements.append(entry)

    bounds = [*lo, *hi] if elements else [0.0] * 6
    return {"elements": elements, "bounds": bounds}


def write(model_path: str | Path, out_path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Build the mesh and write it compactly — this file ships to the browser."""
    p = Path(out_path)
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_text(json.dumps(build(model_path), separators=(",", ":")), encoding="utf-8")
    return p
=== publish.py ===
"""Turn a completed run into the Studio's static payload.

The Studio is a static site. It cannot run Python, call the pipeline, or hold a
secret, so everything it needs must already be a file: the mesh, the sheet, the
verdict, the plan, the source. This module copies exactly those into `web/data/`
and writes the index the Studio reads on load.

Keeping this separate from the run itself matters -- a run produces artifacts
whether or not anyone ever looks at them, and publishing is a deliberate second
step that can be pointed at a different directory or skipped entirely.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
WEB_DATA = REPO_ROOT / "web" / "data"

# What the Studio actually loads, and what it does without if a file is absent.
WANTED = {
    "mesh.json": "3D view",
    "verdict.json": "findings",
    "plan.json": "the plan the agent returned",
    "design.py": "the building as code",
}


def slug(s: str) -> str:
    out = "".join(c.lower() if c.isalnum() else "-" for c in s)
    while "--" in out:
        out = out.replace("--", "-")
    return out.strip("-") or "project"


def publish_candidate(cand_dir: Path, dest: Path) -> dict:
    """Copy one candidate's artifacts into the site and describe what landed."""
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    present: list[str] = []
    for name in WANTED:
        src = cand_dir / name
        if src.is_file():
            shutil.copy2(src, dest / name)
            present.append(name)

    # The sheet lives under pkg/sheets/ with a storey-dependent name; the Studio
    # only ever shows the first, so normalise it to one predictable filename.
    sheets = sorted((cand_dir / "pkg" / "sheets").glob("*.svg")) if (cand_dir / "pkg").is_dir() else []
    if not sheets:
        sheets = sorted(cand_dir.glob("**/*.svg"))
    if sheets:
        shutil.copy2(sheets[0], dest / "sheet.svg")
        present.append("sheet.svg")
    pdfs = sorted((cand_dir / "pkg" / "sheets").glob("*.pdf")) if (cand_dir / "pkg").is_dir() else []
    if pdfs:
        shutil.copy2(pdfs[0], dest / "sheet.pdf")
        present.append("sheet.pdf")

    verdict = {}
    vp = dest / "verdict.json"
    if vp.is_file():
        verdict = json.loads(vp.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return {
        "name": cand_dir.name,
        "files": present,
        "ok": bool(verdict.get("ok")),
        "checked": verdict.get("checked", 0),
        "failed": verdict.get("failed", 0),
        "not_evaluated": verdict.get("not_evaluated", 0),
        "blocking_failures": verdict.get("blocking_failures", 0),
        "metrics": verdict.get("metrics", {}),
    }


def publish_run(run_dir: Path, *, project: str, web_data: Path = WEB_DATA,
                brief: Path | None = None, log=print) -> Path:
    """Publish every candidate of one run, then refresh the site index."""
    run_json = run_dir / "run.json"
    run = json.loads(run_json.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if run_json.is_file() else {}
    key = slug(project)
    dest_root = web_data / key
    if dest_root.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(dest_root)      # a republish replaces, never merges
    dest_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    cands: list[dict] = []
    for cand in sorted(p for p in run_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        entry = publish_candidate(cand, dest_root / cand.name)
        meta = next((c for c in run.get("candidates", []) if c.get("name") == cand.name), {})
        entry["label"] = meta.get("label", cand.name)
        entry["error"] = meta.get("error", "")
        cands.append(entry)
        log(f"  · {cand.name}: {', '.join(entry['files']) or 'nothing to publish'}")

    if brief and Path(brief).is_file():
        shutil.copy2(brief, dest_root / "brief.json")

    (dest_root / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps({
        "project": project,
        "engine": run.get("engine", "local"),
        "winner": run.get("winner", ""),
        "critic": run.get("critic", ""),
        "candidates": cands,
    }, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

    _write_index(web_data)
    return dest_root


def _write_index(web_data: Path) -> Path:
    """List every published project so the Studio can offer them on load."""
    projects = []
    for d in sorted(p for p in web_data.iterdir() if p.is_dir()) if web_data.is_dir() else []:
        rj = d / "run.json"
        if not rj.is_file():
            continue
        run = json.loads(rj.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        winner = next((c for c in run.get("candidates", []) if c["name"] == run.get("winner")), None)
        projects.append({
            "key": d.name,
            "project": run.get("project", d.name),
            "winner": run.get("winner", ""),
            "engine": run.get("engine", ""),
            "candidates": len(run.get("candidates", [])),
            "ok": bool(winner and winner.get("ok")),
            "checked": (winner or {}).get("checked", 0),
            "not_evaluated": (winner or {}).get("not_evaluated", 0),
            "failed": (winner or {}).get("failed", 0),
        })
    p = web_data / "index.json"
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    p.write_text(json.dumps({"projects": projects}, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    return p

Stacked on #9. Adds the product UI, plus the mesh/publish pipeline it needs, and rewrites the README around the product.

![result view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/placeholder)

## What it is

Five questions in → a 3D model, a dimensioned sheet, and a compliance report citing the statute behind every finding. **No backend, no build step, no secret in the browser.**

```
web/index.html   brief · working · result · options
web/studio.css   brand tokens + layout
web/studio.js    interview, Three.js viewer, result panes
```

## Brand: carried forward, not reinvented

The drawing-office palette in `ui/static/style.css` was already right for this domain, so the Studio uses the same tokens (`--board`, `--paper`, `--accent #2A62D8`, `--pass/--warn/--fail`, Familjen Grotesk + IBM Plex Mono). Three rules hold it together:

1. **The drawing is the hero** — panels stay quiet, the sheet and model get the contrast.
2. **Every number is monospace.** Areas, widths, thresholds and tags all line up.
3. **Verdict colour is reserved.** Nothing decorative is ever green.

## The interview is short on purpose

Five questions, and only the ones a `tier: law` rule actually needs are blocking. Each states the rule that asks for it — question 2 says outright that **BayBO Art. 48** is why it wants the number of homes.

Everything else gets a default shown as an **assumption chip with its reason**:

```
ceiling height 2.50 m · BayBO Art. 45 (1) minimum 2.40 m + 100 mm build-up
```

The silent default is the failure mode this product exists to remove, so there isn't one.

## 3D: mesh.json, not in-browser IFC

Taken from the viewer on the `studio` branch and moved into the pipeline. `ifcopenshell.geom` triangulates once, when the artifact is produced, carrying tag / class / storey / area per element so the viewer needs nothing else.

| | mesh.json + Three.js | web-ifc (WASM) |
|---|---|---|
| Payload | **13 kB** per building | the whole IFC |
| Tags and areas | carried in the JSON | must be re-derived |
| Server at view time | **none** | none |

84 kB per candidate total. That is what makes the Studio a static file reading a static file.

## The demo to look at

`dreifamilienhaus` — three dwellings **trigger BayBO Art. 48**, DIN 18040-2 becomes mandatory, and the `linear` candidate now **FAILS** on a 1.15 m corridor that was merely advisory for the single-family house. The guidance-tier room width beside it still doesn't block.

=====PR9=====
## The industry and its loop

**Architecture.** An architect's detailing work goes out and someone finds out months later whether it was right. But building code is *machine-checkable* — room heights, daylight ratios, door widths, corridor clearances are all decidable from a model. That is the loop, and it already exists; nothing was sitting inside it.

This PR is the layer that puts Devin inside it.

```
brief ──▶ N strategies ──▶ build each ──▶ verify each ──▶ merge the winner
              (Devin)        (0 tokens)      (the gate)      (no human)
```

## Autonomy — nobody in the middle

The human is at the **trigger**, never inside the run. Once a brief is sealed the pipeline runs to a merged PR with **no approval step**. There is no Approve button: `recognition.score` is the only gate, and `score.rank` picks the winner from the compliance result. Trigger via `repository_dispatch`, the Actions tab, or just committing a brief to `briefs/`.

## Verification — it knows good from bad by itself

A model can never report its own success here. Devin returns an `ArchitectPlan` (areas and adjacencies) and **never touches the repo**; the artifacts it is judged on are produced downstream by deterministic code. So "I fixed it" is not something a session can assert.

Four independent checks: the cited rule engine, geometry sanity, contract validation at every boundary, and pytest.

## Artifacts — usable by the industry

Per candidate: `model.ifc` (IFC4 with real `IfcSpace`/`IfcWall`/openings), dimensioned floor-plan sheets in **SVG/PDF/PNG/DXF**, room/door/window schedules, and `verdict.json` with a citation on every finding. Opens in Revit or AutoCAD.

## Not wired to one prepared example

Any `DesignBrief` works. Two are included (`familienhaus`, `dreifamilienhaus`); the second has 3 dwellings, which **auto-triggers BayBO Art. 48** → DIN 18040-2 becomes mandatory and the *same* corridor finding flips from advisory to blocking. Nobody configured that — the rule declares its own trigger.

## How the approach changed while building

I started intending a clarifying-question interview. The challenge is explicit that a human in the loop makes a copilot, so the interview moved to *before* the trigger and the run became sealed. That turned out better: the assumption register makes every inferred value visible without anyone approving anything.

Second change: Devin was going to push branches. It has no write access to this repo (the standing 403). Rather than wait on a settings change, Devin now returns a plan and **we** build it — which is the safer split anyway, for the reason in Verification above.

## What the gate caught

Run against a real Devin session (9-room house): the plan was **rejected once by the schema** (`via: "opening"` is not `"open"`), repaired automatically, rebuilt, and passed at **60 checked · 2 not evaluated · 0 failed**.

It also surfaced two latent bugs in the existing codebase:

The dreifamilienhaus data confirms the branch's headline demo: with 3 dwellings, BayBO Art. 48 triggers DIN 18040-2 and the `linear` candidate genuinely fails on a blocking corridor finding while its siblings pass. The review is complete — here it is.

---

# Review: Recognition, as it stands on `feat/studio-ui`

**TLDR:** The product is real and it works — I ran the full test suite (55 passed) and the advertised `autopilot` command end-to-end on your machine, and both are green. Your authorship setup is already correct, so pushes will be yours. The actual problem is not the code: **the entire product is stranded on a PR stack that never reaches `main`**, GitHub Pages isn't enabled, and the autopilot's self-merge in CI is blocked by one repository setting. Nothing ships until those three things are decided. There's also meaningful doc/instruction drift and two older UI implementations whose fate needs a call from you.

## Your account setup (checked first, since you raised it)

- `git` commits as `0-uddeshya-0 <uddeshyasingh.de@gmail.com>`, and I verified via the GitHub API that this email attributes commits to the **0-uddeshya-0** account (the existing commits show `author.login: 0-uddeshya-0`).
- `gh` is authenticated as **0-uddeshya-0** with `repo` + `workflow` scopes, so pushes and settings changes go through your account.
- The Claude-account email in this session (pateluddeshya2003@…) appears nowhere in git config — nothing will be authored as your teammate. I saved these facts to project memory so future sessions don't have to re-verify.

## What I verified by running it

- `uv run pytest -q` → **55 passed** in ~23 s (only benign shapely `oriented_envelope` warnings).
- `uv run recognition autopilot briefs/familienhaus.json` → 3 candidates, all PASS, winner `open` (usable ratio 0.862), exactly as the README promises.
- The published `web/data/dreifamilienhaus/run.json` backs PR #11's demo claim: `linear` fails with 1 blocking finding once Art. 48 triggers DIN 18040-2; `compact`/`open` pass.

## How the system hangs together

Two product stages coexist in this branch. Stage 1 (the original "detailing engineer": IFC in → schedules/sheets/compliance out, via `recognition run|check`, with the FastAPI copilot UI in `ui/`). Stage 2 (the current product: brief in → `autopilot` fans out 3 strategies → Devin returns an `ArchitectPlan` with **no coordinates** → `translate.py` deterministically packs rooms and emits `design.py` → `design.py` builds IFC4 → `rules.py` + `score.py` gate it with cited, tiered rules → the scorer picks the winner → `publish.py` drops static artifacts into `web/data/` for the zero-backend Studio). The anti-hallucination split (model plans, code draws, deterministic gate decides) is genuinely enforced in code, not just described — contract validation errors are written as repair instructions and fed back to Devin sessions, and the tests assert exactly these properties.

## Findings, most important first

**1. Nothing is on `main` — and the stack never gets there.** `origin/main` has 4 scaffold commits. The product is 27 commits ahead on this chain: [PR #11](https://github.com/0-uddeshya-0/Recognition/pull/11) (`feat/studio-ui` → `feat/autonomous-layer`) → [PR #9](https://github.com/0-uddeshya-0/Recognition/pull/9) (→ `poc/design-as-code`) → **no PR exists from `poc/design-as-code` toward `main`**. Merging the whole stack as-is would still leave everything short of `main`. Your branch contains the full useful history (including the `ui/poc` line); it does *not* contain the `studio` branch (PRs #8/#10 — the server-based Studio with the plain-words chat via Claude) or PR #1's earlier parallel attempt.

**2. Deploy is two switches away, both off.** `pages.yml` is correct and honest (it refuses to deploy if `web/data/index.json` is missing), but it only triggers on pushes to `main`, and **GitHub Pages is not enabled on the repo** (API returns 404). So "deploy" = merge to main + enable Pages (Source: GitHub Actions). The repo is public, so the Studio would be publicly visible at `https://0-uddeshya-0.github.io/Recognition/`.

**3. The autopilot's autonomy breaks at the last step in CI.** The only real run ([32593249845](https://github.com/0-uddeshya-0/Recognition/actions/runs/32593249845)) designed, verified, and pushed `design/familienhaus-…` — then died at `gh pr create`: *"GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests."* That's the repo setting `can_approve_pull_request_reviews` (currently `false`). Additionally, [autopilot.yml](.github/workflows/autopilot.yml) uses `gh pr merge --admin`, which the Actions token can't do even after the setting flips — it should be a plain `--squash` (there's no branch protection). The Devin secrets are already configured, so the `devin` engine can run in CI once this is fixed.

**4. The repo's instructions to agents contradict the product.** [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and [REVIEW.md](REVIEW.md) still describe stage 1 only ("You never edit the design… an IFC model goes in") — any agent (Devin, Claude, Codex) onboarding from them gets the wrong story. Smaller drift in the same family: [docs/architecture/README.md](docs/architecture/README.md) L7 still says web-ifc parses IFC in the browser (superseded by the mesh.json approach that [studio.md](docs/architecture/studio.md) correctly describes); studio.md's "live run via `repository_dispatch` from the browser" isn't implemented in `studio.js` (it hands you the brief + CLI command instead — honest, but the spec should match); the README's sample output numbers are stale (says `open — 48 checked`, current runs give 54); and PR #11's body has a literal `placeholder` screenshot link where AGENTS.md requires real imagery.

**5. Three UIs exist; only one is the product.** The static `web/` Studio (this branch), the legacy `ui/` FastAPI copilot (still tested, still in `pyproject.toml` with its fastapi/uvicorn/jinja2 dependencies), and the unmerged `studio` branch Studio (building-as-code editor + chat-driven edits through Claude — its mesh viewer was already ported into the pipeline, the chat was deliberately dropped). Whether `ui/` and the `studio` branch have a future is a product decision, not a code one.

**6. Minor code nits** (none blocking): re-submitting the Studio interview appends a duplicate download-row (`studio.js:558`); the brief's project name is hardcoded `"Neubau"` (`studio.js:191`); dead `exclude` logic in `_nearest_neighbour` ([translate.py:426](recognition/translate.py:426)); local `main` is 1 commit behind `origin/main` (trivial fast-forward).

One process note: per your global rules I verified against ground truth (live API state, actual runs) rather than the repo's docs — the docs' "Devin can't write to the repo" blocker, for instance, is **moot now**: the architecture changed so Devin never pushes, which the autonomy doc itself notes.

result.output:
# Complete Guidance on Instructing Devin Effectively

## Core Principle
The foundational instruction is to **"be as specific as possible,"** treating Devin like you would a colleague requiring a detailed specification.

## Effective Prompt Structure

The document provides an example prompt demonstrating best practices:
- Establishing context (the Devin repo, broader purpose)
- Providing step-by-step tasks broken into logical parts
- Defining clear success criteria (e.g., "emit a specific event upon 80% usage")
- Referencing existing patterns and established code approaches

## Key Do's and Don'ts

**Opacity & Specificity:**
- **Do:** Make decisions for Devin; offer "specific design choices and implementation strategies"
- **Don't:** Leave decisions open-ended or make vague requests like "Improve our database's performance"

**Leverage Strengths:**
- **Do:** Assign tasks aligned with Devin's capabilities; provide examples, modules, and direct documentation links
- **Do:** Reference specific files and use MCP integrations for Figma, databases, and monitoring tools
- **Don't:** Omit context for complex tasks requiring domain knowledge

**Feedback Loops:**
- **Do:** "Establish clear and frequent checks" using tests, build validations, and lint checks
- **Do:** Enable Devin Review with Auto-Fix for iterative PR improvement
- **Don't:** Assign tasks without defining evaluation methods

**Checkpoints:**
- **Do:** Break complex tasks into "smaller checkpoints" and "verifiable sub-tasks"
- **Do:** Define success explicitly (e.g., "verify the endpoint returns status 200")
- **Don't:** Use vague success criteria like "Make sure it works"

## Devin's Testing Capabilities
Devin should test its own work using available desktop tools: running applications, browser testing, visual verification at multiple widths, and screen recordings before opening PRs.

## Reusable Frameworks
- **Playbooks:** For step-by-step procedures tied to specific, repetitive tasks
- **Knowledge:** For persistent context like coding standards, common bugs, deployment workflows

The distinction: "Use Playbooks for step-by-step procedures tied to specific tasks. Use Knowledge for general tips, conventions, and context that apply broadly across sessions."

124	    def _launch(self, job: Job, trigger: str, instruction: str | None, rules_yaml: str | None) -> None:
125	        if job.status == "running":
126	            raise EngineError("A run is already in progress.")
127	        run = job.new_run(trigger, instruction, rules_yaml)
128	        job.reset_steps(LOCAL_STEPS)
129	        t = threading.Thread(target=self._worker, args=(job, run), daemon=True, name=f"run-{job.id}-{run.index}")
130	        t.start()

132	    def _command(self, job: Job, run: Run) -> list[str]:
133	        cmd = [self.python, "-m", "recognition.cli", "run", job.model_path, run.out_dir, "--project", job.project]
134	        if run.rules_yaml is not None:
135	            rules_path = Path(run.out_dir) / "rules.yaml"
136	            rules_path.write_text(run.rules_yaml, encoding="utf-8")
137	            cmd += ["--rules", str(rules_path)]

140	    def _worker(self, job: Job, run: Run) -> None:
141	        out = Path(run.out_dir)
142	        job.set_step("Load model", "running", Path(job.model_path).name)
143	        try:
144	            proc = subprocess.Popen(self._command(job, run), cwd=REPO_ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
145	                                    stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
146	        except OSError as e:
147	            job.fail_run(run, f"could not start pipeline: {e}")
148	            return
149	        while proc.poll() is None:
150	            self._tick(job, out)
151	            time.sleep(self.poll_interval)
152	        self._tick(job, out)
153	        _, err = proc.communicate()
154	        summary_p = out / "summary.json"
155	        if proc.returncode == 0 and summary_p.exists():
156	            summary = json.loads(summary_p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
157	            self._final_details(job, summary)
158	            job.finish_run(run, summary)
159	        else:
160	            tail = "\n".join((err or "").strip().splitlines()[-8:]) or f"pipeline exited with {proc.returncode}"
161	            job.fail_run(run, tail)
162	
163	    @staticmethod
164	    def _tick(job: Job, out: Path) -> None:
165	        """Advance steps from what the pipeline has written so far (it writes in this order)."""
166	        if (out / "schedules").exists():
167	            job.set_step("Load model", "done")
168	            job.set_step("Schedules", "running" if not (out / "report.json").exists() else "done")
169	        if (out / "report.json").exists():
170	            job.set_step("Schedules", "done")
171	            if job.step("Compliance").status != "done":
172	                try:
173	                    s = json.loads((out / "report.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["summary"]
174	                    job.set_step("Compliance", "done", f"{s['checks']} checks · {s['errors']} errors · {s['warnings']} warnings")
175	                except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
176	                    job.set_step("Compliance", "running")
177	            job.set_step("Sheets", "running" if job.step("Sheets").status == "pending" else job.step("Sheets").status)
178	        sheets = out / "sheets"
179	        if sheets.exists():
180	            pngs = sorted(p.stem for p in sheets.glob("*.png"))
181	            if pngs and job.step("Sheets").status != "done":
182	                job.set_step("Sheets", "running", " · ".join(p.split("_", 1)[0] for p in pngs))
183	        if (out / "model.detailed.ifc").exists():
184	            job.set_step("Sheets", "done")
185	            job.set_step("Enriched IFC", "running")
186	        if (out / "summary.json").exists():
187	            job.set_step("Enriched IFC", "done")
188	
189	    @staticmethod
190	    def _final_details(job: Job, summary: dict) -> None:
191	        c = summary["counts"]
192	        job.set_step("Load model", "done", f"{c['storeys']} storeys · {c['walls']} walls · {c['spaces']} rooms · "
193	                                           f"{c['doors']} doors · {c['windows']} windows")
194	        s = summary["schedules"]
195	        job.set_step("Schedules", "done", f"{s['rooms']} rooms · {s['doors']} doors · {s['windows']} windows")
196	        job.set_step("Sheets", "done", " · ".join(f"{sh['sheet']} {sh['storey']}" for sh in summary["sheets"]))
197	        job.set_step("Enriched IFC", "done", summary["files"]["enriched_ifc"])

254	def github_repo() -> str:
255	    """owner/name of the origin remote, unless GITHUB_REPO overrides it."""
256	    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_REPO"):
257	        return os.environ["GITHUB_REPO"]
258	    try:
259	        url = subprocess.check_output(["git", "remote", "get-url", "origin"], cwd=REPO_ROOT, text=True).strip()
260	    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
